claims.statement: Asana issues OAuth refresh tokens: long-lived tokens returned when an authorization code is exchanged, used at the token exchange endpoint to obtain new access tokens until the user deauthorizes the app.

sources.supports: If exchanging a `code`, this is a long-lived token that can be used to get new access tokens when older ones expire

claims.statement: Asana states its API tokens, including OAuth refresh tokens, should be treated as opaque and that token formats may change without notice; the documentation states no prefix, alphabet or length.

sources.supports: Asana API tokens should be treated as opaque. Token formats may change without notice. This applies to any Asana API tokens, including: personal access tokens, service account tokens, and both OAuth refresh tokens and access tokens.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Candidate is not researched beyond existence: the format (prefix, alphabet, length, checksum) is not recorded and has not been researched by research-family.

The documentation states no literal format for a refresh token (the token exchange example response uses an obviously illustrative string). An official page stating one would be needed before any contract is written.
